hard_case: `t["assert"].equal` runs the same loose (`==`) comparison as `t.assert.equal`; the spec read no assertion through a computed member before RIPR-SPEC-0252 rule 1 accepted a string-literal key (2026-10-14)

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; tsx 4.23.15; node:test + node:assert (built in); edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 4 days give 6 instead of 5

reasoning: The test asserts `t["assert"].equal(holdFee(4), 5)`; the edit adds two, so 6 is compared with 5 and the test fails. RIPR-SPEC-0252 rule 1 (amended 2026-10-14) reads a string-literal computed member `t["assert"]` as `t.assert`, so the assertion is exact_value / strong and the finding reads `credited`. Before the amendment the computed member read no assertion and the row was a false actionable gap.
